## Bio
Growing up, the bill was scarier than the illness. My family immigrated without 
health insurance, so regular medical visits were out of reach. When my dad had a 
heart attack, I couldn't stop wondering: "If we'd had insurance, would this have 
happened at all?" That question never left me and has shaped my
career interest to be in preventive cardiology and immigrant health. 

Currently, I am a part-time MPH student at the Johns Hopkins School of Public 
Health, concentrating in Epidemiology and Biostatistics. I hope to become a 
clinician and clinical epidemiologist who uses population-level research to 
improve cardiovascular outcomes for immigrant and underserved communities. 
I’m particularly interested in hypertension management, novel biomarkers, and 
community outreach. 

Please download my CV to get details of my research, clinical, and public health experience
